title: U.S. House · Oregon's 4th District
area: Southwestern Oregon, including Eugene/Springfield, the central coast, and the counties along the California border west of the Cascades.

context.text: Incumbent Val Hoyle defeated Melissa Bird and Dan Bahlen with 75.1% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. Monique DeSpain defeated Stefan Strek 86.6%-12.4% in the Republican primary. DeSpain also won the Libertarian ballot line and Justin Filip is the Pacific Green Party and Progressive Party nominee.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 statement on ICE detention plans in Oregon, said she opposes spending more money on a larger ICE presence in the state.
positions.quote: We don’t need more money wasted on having a larger ICE presence here to harass, intimidate and detain hardworking Oregonians based on the color of their skin.

positions.summary: Her official issues page says she is a member of the House Pro-Choice Caucus and that the government should not get in the middle of personal health care decisions.
positions.quote: I understand how critical it is for all people to have access to safe and effective reproductive care.

positions.summary: Her official issues page says she is fighting to protect and improve Medicare and Medicaid.
positions.quote: Every day I am fighting to protect and improve our most vital programs, including Medicare and Medicaid.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Subcommittees on Indian and Insular Affairs; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Subcommittees on Highways and Transit; Water Resources and Environment).

candidates.name: Monique DeSpain

priorities.text: Public safety and homelessness: says the district has seen 'rampant homelessness, unsafe streets, rising costs' and calls for law-enforcement collaboration and addiction/mental-illness-focused solutions to homelessness.
Border security: says she supports 'constant vigilance to stop the flow of human trafficking, fentanyl, and other deadly drugs' into the country.
Government spending: says she would end what she calls 'reckless tax-and-spend policies fueling inflation.'

positions.summary: Says she will oppose any effort in Congress to limit or restrict abortion access for Oregonians.
positions.quote: I will oppose any effort in Congress to limit or restrict abortion access for Oregonians.

positions.summary: Says noncitizens who commit serious violent crimes or trafficking should be removed, and that she supports border barriers and a staffed Border Patrol; says mass deportation is not a realistic solution and supports a one-time path to lawful status for long-settled, non-criminal residents.
positions.quote: Indiscriminate mass deportation is neither a realistic nor constructive solution.

positions.summary: Says she supports ending permitting costs, building regulations and land-use restrictions that limit new construction.
positions.quote: I support ending prohibitive and inflationary policies that stifle new construction with excessive permitting costs, building regulations, city and county codes, bureaucratic red tape, and outdated land-use restrictions imposed by the government itself.

statements.quote: I will support a Parents’ Bill of Rights to ensure real transparency and accountability: full access to curricula, clear reporting on school performance, and genuine school choice.
statements.context: On her campaign website, Education page

statements.quote: It is my goal to ensure they have the necessary authority and resources to do their job effectively, from Customs and Border Patrol to our local sheriffs, police, and district attorneys.
statements.context: On her campaign website, Public Safety and Crime page

statements.quote: Consumers and businesses—not distant bureaucrats—should decide when and how to adopt alternative energy options, free from prohibitive costs or forced transitions.
statements.context: On her campaign website, Energy page

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements are from the Priorities page of her campaign website. She did not state a position on several guide issues (rent, taxes, tariffs, minimum wage); her Israel and election-integrity pages do not map to the guide statements on military aid or proof of citizenship.

candidates.name: Justin Filip

priorities.text: His 2024 campaign website stated his top priorities as ending U.S. military involvement in the conflict in Gaza and reducing military spending, bringing federal dollars to the district to address housing and homelessness, protecting federal lands, and advancing high-speed rail in the Pacific Northwest.
In July 2026 Eugene Weekly reported his priorities as ending U.S. imperialism, addressing homelessness, improving health care and protecting the environment.

positions.summary: In OPB's October 2024 candidate questionnaire (from his 2024 run), said he would support codifying reproductive rights in law.
positions.quote: No. I believe in women’s reproductive rights and I would support codifying it in law.

positions.summary: In OPB's October 2024 candidate questionnaire (from his 2024 run), called for an arms embargo on Israel until the occupation of Gaza and the West Bank ends.
positions.quote: We must put an arms embargo in place until Israel ends the occupation of Gaza and the West Bank.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements are from OPB's 2024 candidate questionnaire (verbatim answers), since no 2026 campaign site or questionnaire was found; his positions may have changed. Eugene Weekly (July 2026) paraphrases his priorities. Positions and statements come from OPB's October 2024 candidate questionnaire and have not been confirmed for 2026.

statements.quote: I support the right to seek asylum and a path to citizenship for our immigrant neighbors. I would not support any bill that would infringe on that.
statements.context: In OPB's October 2024 candidate questionnaire (from his 2024 run)

statements.quote: We need to listen to the experts who have studied the science and take strong action to protect our environment.
statements.context: In OPB's October 2024 candidate questionnaire (from his 2024 run)
